newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila bourse confident on self-regulatory status.
newsitem.headline: Manila bourse confident on self-regulatory status.

text.p: The Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) said on Thursday it is confident it will be granted a permanent self-regulatory organisation (SRO) status by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).
In a statement, the PSE said that the expiration of its temporary SRO status will enable the bourse to hasten efforts to become a full and permanent SRO.
"We have absolutely no doubt that we will achieve this status in partnership with the SEC," the PSE said.
The bourse was granted the temporary SRO last December 16, and that status expired on February 28.

Earlier this month, the PSE was hit by a number of senior-level resignations culminating in the departure of its president Vitaliano Nanagas. The president resigned because of differences with the bourse staff, the exchange said.
SEC Chairman Perfecto Yasay told Reuters in an interview last week that the permanent SRO status will require the bourse to meet some criteria.

These include the revision of some stock listing rules to make them more objective, setting standards for the hiring and firing of top personnel and pursuing investigations on insider trading, price manipulation and other violations of SEC rules.
The stock exchange, however, did not say in the statement if it has met any of the conditions set by the regulatory body.
Instead, the PSE said it has "instituted wide-ranging reforms and taken steps to stiumlate the Philippine capital market".
It also cited an increase in stock market trading volume and a rise in market capitalisation as among its gains.
